rule: Test transition grammar under aggressive input for flashing and skipped perceptual states.
why: Repeated light fade/scene fade handoffs can look controlled slowly and flash under scrollbar dragging.
mechanism: Continuous information and luminance handoff across scene boundaries.
whenToUse: Multi-scene fades, large luminance changes or meaningful scroll transformations.
whenNotToUse: Do not suppress user input to hide an unsafe transition; static pages need no scene governor.
parameters: Handoff overlap, luminance contrast, event repetition and state-path continuity.
dependencies: Actual rendered sequences and fast-input controls.
implementationPattern: Review a stable base layer through handoffs.
Coordinate outgoing and incoming light/state sources.
Avoid repeating full-field fade pulses when several boundaries are crossed at once.

goodExample.claim: VELORUM refinement preserved forward/reverse peak state in numerical checks.

antiExample.claim: LAMELLA repeated light fades flashed under aggressive scrollbar dragging in Human Review.

repairStrategy: Use a shared continuous handoff or stable base layer.
Reduce repeated luminance pulses while preserving the intended signature contrast.
Review the worst boundary frame and reduced-motion handoff.
cost: Sequence capture and boundary review; technique dependent rendering cost.

provenance.claim: Candidate operationalization of existing human/technical experiment evidence; transfer unvalidated.
HEG/TEG specification and Human Authority boundary.

transferability: Observed context only; weaker-model and cross-domain transfer TO VALIDATE.
